Open a Kubernetes session

Source: R/kube.R
Kube.Rd

Returns a Kube object - a thin wrapper over ApiClient and DynamicClient that lets you write idiomatic R against the cluster without touching the typed V1* model classes:

Usage

kube(
  config_file = NULL,
  context = NULL,
  namespace = NULL,
  client = NULL,
  field_manager = "rk8s"
)

Arguments

config_file

Passed to load_kube_config().

context

Passed to load_kube_config().

namespace

Default namespace for verbs that take one. NULL (default) uses the kubeconfig context's namespace, falling back to "default".

client

Optional pre-built ApiClient. When given, config_file and context are ignored.

field_manager

Field manager used by kube_apply() (defaults to "rk8s").

Value

A Kube object.

Details


k <- kube()                                   # ~/.kube/config
kube_get(k, "pods", namespace = "default")
kube_apply(k, "deployment.yaml")
kube_logs(k, "nginx-abc", namespace = "default")
kube_delete(k, "deployment/nginx", namespace = "default")
kube_scale(k, "deployment", "nginx", replicas = 5, namespace = "default")
kube_watch(k, "pods", on_event = function(type, obj)
             message(type, " ", obj$metadata$name))

This is the high-level surface most users want. The typed classes (V1Pod, CoreV1Api, ...) and the DynamicClient still work and are there when you need them - Kube is built on top of both.

Resource references can be:

  • a kind alias: "pod", "pods", "po", "deployment", "deploy", "svc", ...

  • "kind/name": "deployment/nginx"

  • an explicit apiVersion+kind: "apps/v1:Deployment"

  • a c(api_version, kind) vector: c("apps/v1", "Deployment")

Constructed via kube(). Carries an ApiClient, a DynamicClient, a default namespace, and a kind-to-resource alias table.

Usually you don't call Kube methods directly; use the kube_* verbs which dispatch into here.

Public fields

client

The backing ApiClient.

dynamic

The backing DynamicClient.

namespace

Default namespace.

field_manager

Field manager used by kube_apply().

Method resource()

Resolve a resource ref to a DynamicResource. Accepts: "pod", "pods", "po", "deployment/nginx" (name is captured separately via parse_ref), "apps/v1:Deployment", or a c(api_version, kind) vector.

Usage

Kube$resource(ref)

Arguments

ref

Resource reference.

Method resource_and_name()

Parse ref and return both the resource and a name (if one was embedded as "kind/name").

Usage

Kube$resource_and_name(ref)

Arguments

ref

Resource reference.

Method clone()

The objects of this class are cloneable with this method.

Usage

Kube$clone(deep = FALSE)

Arguments

deep

Whether to make a deep clone.
